chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Yaqub ibn Shu'ayb, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the tenth (ushr) which is taken from the man, 'Can one reckon with it to be from his zakat?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, if he so desires.'

key_terms.أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah (Imam al-Sadiq peace be upon him)
key_terms.الْعُشُورِ: The tenth part, a tax levied on goods or produce
key_terms.يَحْتَسِبُ: To reckon or count towards a debt/obligation

ai.seo_question: Can government taxes be counted as Zakat in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the flexibility in Islamic fiscal jurisprudence by allowing individuals to offset their obligatory *zakat* with the *ushr* (tithe) collected by the ruling authority. This ruling highlights the scholarly distinction between the mandatory nature of *zakat* and the discretionary or administrative nature of state taxes, emphasizing that the fulfillment of the religious duty depends on the payer's intention and the nature of the levy. It underscores the principle that financial obligations to the state can serve as valid substitutes for spiritual dues when the authority acts within its legitimate scope.
